name: Evangeline Moss
appearance: A gentle-faced woman of thirty-eight in the plain grey habit and wheat-gold sash of a Fertility Order lay sister. Her hands are a midwife's hands — strong, quick, always warm. Mud from the parish garden never quite leaves her hem, and dried flowers hang from her belt in bundles that change with the moon.

visualProfile.symmetry: Warm, motherly; unremarkable until she smiles
visualProfile.hairStyle: Light brown, hidden beneath her habit's coif
visualProfile.gait: Brisk, purposeful, hands free for catching things
visualProfile.distinctMarks: Midwife's calluses; soil permanently under the nails
visualProfile.clothing: Grey Fertility Order habit, wheat-gold sash, flower bundles on her belt

faction: Church of the Earth Mother (Fertility Order, lay sister)
storyRelevance: Evangeline took the Planter potion with her bishop's blessing after fifteen years delivering babies and burying infants in equal measure. Her garden now grows medicines no apothecary can match — and last month, unsupervised, grew something with too many joints. The Earth Mother's church is delighted with her progress and evasive about the thing in the compost. She has begun dreaming of seeds that scream when planted wrong.
goals: Master growth without letting it master her. Deliver the O'Donnell twins safely. Understand what her garden is becoming — and decide whether the church's silence about it is discretion or permission.
disposition: Nurturing, patient, quietly stubborn. Handles birth, death, and bishops with the same unhurried competence. Grieves quickly and thoroughly, then plants something.
voice: Soft rural Loen accent, steady as rainfall. Talks to plants, patients, and problems identically.
personality: The Planter creed — cultivate, don't force — matches both her faith and her temperament. Her risk is not ambition but abundance: everything she tends grows past its borders, including her sense of what counts as acceptable harvest.
exampleOutput: [**Evangeline**]: She snaps off a leaf and smells it, frowning. "This bed's been watered with something that isn't water." A pause; her voice gentles. "It's all right to tell me. Whatever's feeding my garden, I'd rather know it than guess it."
haunt: The parish garden behind Harvest Chapel and the birthing rooms of Cherwood Borough

drives.coreWant: To make things grow that should grow — and know the difference
drives.sessionWant: Deliver the twins safely and identify what fed her garden
drives.sceneWant: Leave every living thing she touches better than she found it

short: Check the strange bed before dawn dew burns off
Boil water and lay out the birthing kit
Pray the evening office among the beehives
medium: Advance toward Druid under proper supervision
Confront the bishop about the compost thing, gently
Build a greenhouse the neighbors won't ask about
wants.long: Become the Earth Mother's quiet hand in Backlund — healer first, horror never.

equipment: Bundles of drying herbs (some shouldn't exist)
Watering can that never quite empties
Prayer beads of carved apple wood
The parish ledger of births and deaths in her careful hand

characterProfile.name: Evangeline Moss
skills: Plant Cultivation — grow medicines no apothecary can match
Enhanced Healing Touch — mend flesh with a hand laid gently
Growth Sense — feel what the garden is becoming
characterProfile.notes: Earth Mother Planter whose healing garden produces medicines and one troubling thing in the compost.
